## Problem

`.apm/instructions/master.instructions.md` §3 last bullet (line 40) currently reads:

> After each merge, run a retrospective.

This leaves issue creation to operator memory, which contradicts the same section's other bullet:

> Push deterministic work into hooks, pre-commit, and CI/CD …

In practice, retrospectives get skipped because nothing in the harness forces them to surface. The rule should state that the retrospective **issue** is auto-opened, so the principle is co-located with the deterministic-harness requirement and the follow-up CI work has a clear spec to satisfy.

## Scope of this issue

**Spec-text change only.** Update the source line in `.apm/instructions/master.instructions.md`, regenerate `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` via `apm compile`. No new workflow, no new label, no `.claude/settings.json` hook.

Proposed wording (replaces the single existing bullet):

```
- After each merge, auto-open a retrospective issue — make this deterministic, not operator-memory.
```

## Out of scope (deferred to follow-up issues)

- GitHub Actions workflow that actually creates the issue on PR-merge to the default branch.
- New `retrospective` label, or routing rules in `docs/issue-triage.md`.
- Issue body template / retrospective runbook (`docs/retrospective.md` — referenced as Phase 8 in #63).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `.apm/instructions/master.instructions.md` line 40 updated as above.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` regenerated via `uv run --with "apm-cli==0.12.1" apm compile`; `verify-apm-drift.yml` is green.
- [ ] `git diff --stat` on the PR shows changes confined to `master.instructions.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` (plus `README.md` if APM templates it from the same source).
- [ ] §3 reads naturally end-to-end after the change (no orphan reference to a non-existent workflow).

## Scope

`subscribe_pr_activity` ingests issue/PR content into Claude sessions. Non-ASCII (Japanese, emoji, zero-width, RTL, fullwidth) is a known prompt-injection carrier; `docs/rulesets.md` lines 48-51 already flag it but only as a procedural warning. This umbrella converts that warning into defense-in-depth across three layers:

1. **Past sanitization** — translate JA->EN for ~100 issues + ~50 PRs + 11 issue comments so historical ingestion is ASCII-only.
2. **Write-side detection** — GitHub Action that labels non-ASCII submissions; advisory for the owner, hard-block for external contributors.
3. **Read-side escaping** — developer-local Claude Code `PostToolUse` hook that escapes non-ASCII in `mcp__github__*` responses before Claude consumes them.

## Non-goals

- External translation APIs (translation done by an in-session sub-agent for auditability).
- Modifying compiled `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` content (regenerated by APM).
- Editing third-party comments (none exist today; the repo has a single author).

## Rollout (rationale: ship the bleed-stopper before mopping)

- [ ] **P0** — this tracking issue
- [ ] **P2 first** — `.github/workflows/scan-non-ascii.yml` + new label `severity:non-ascii-content` in `.github/labels.json` + `docs/non-ascii-defense.md` skeleton. Stops new attack surface before the multi-week translation work.
- [ ] **P6 docs** — install steps for the read-side `PostToolUse` hook in `docs/non-ascii-defense.md` (hook itself stays in `$HOME` per `docs/repo-scope.md` #58).
- [ ] **P1 backup** — `gh api --paginate` capture of all 100 issues/PRs + 11 comments, published as Release asset `backup-non-ascii-YYYYMMDD/originals-YYYYMMDD-HHMMZ.json.gz`. SHA-256 recorded below.
- [ ] **P3 translations** — `scripts/translations.json` produced by a read-only sub-agent, lands in a reviewable PR.
- [ ] **P4 checkpoint** — operator approves the translation sample below (10 random + all medium/low-confidence + all severity:security items).
- [ ] **P5 apply** — `scripts/sanitize-history.sh` (bash + jq + `gh api`, mirrors `apply-labels.yml`) executed locally, `--dry-run` first then `--batch-size 10` interactively. Idempotency via SHA-256 of original/translated body; aborts loudly on drift.
- [ ] **P7 retrospective** — auto-opened per CLAUDE.md §3 after this umbrella closes.

## Backup record (filled at P1)

- Release tag: _pending_
- Asset SHA-256: _pending_
- Capture timestamp: _pending_

## Translation review checkpoint (filled at P4)

- [ ] 10 random items (open/closed × issue/PR stratified)
- [ ] All `confidence: medium` items
- [ ] All `confidence: low` items
- [ ] All items labelled `severity:security`

## Rollback paths

- Bad translations -> `scripts/sanitize-history.sh --restore originals-YYYYMMDD.json.gz` (idempotency check makes restore safe).
- Write-side false positives -> revert the workflow file; label stays harmless without the workflow.
- Hook breaks Claude sessions -> operator removes the `PostToolUse` entry from `~/.claude/settings.json`; no repo change.

`subscribe_pr_activity` ingests issue/PR content into Claude sessions. Non-ASCII (Japanese, emoji, zero-width, RTL, fullwidth) is a known prompt-injection carrier; `docs/rulesets.md` lines 48-51 already flag it but only as a procedural warning. This umbrella converts that warning into defense-in-depth across three layers:

1. **Past sanitization** -- translate JA->EN for ~100 issues + ~50 PRs + 11 issue comments so historical ingestion is ASCII-only.
2. **Write-side detection** -- GitHub Action that labels non-ASCII submissions; advisory for the owner, hard-block for external contributors.

Retrospective for [#101](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/101) (closes [#31](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/issues/31)). Filed manually per CLAUDE.md §3 — `auto-open a retrospective issue` — because the workflow that would create it deterministically is still deferred (out-of-scope of #97; see [#100](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/issues/100) "Lift into the harness").

## What changed

- New scheduled workflow `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml`: surveys stale orphan branches weekly (`0 20 * * 0` = 05:00 JST Mon) + `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run` (default `true`) and `min_age_days` (default `60`). Selection: not default branch AND no open PR AND `now − last_commit > min_age_days`.
- New operator runbook `docs/branch-cleanup.md`, patterned after `docs/rulesets.md`.
- **No deletion code path in this PR.** `permissions: contents: read` only; YAML has no `gh api DELETE /git/refs/heads/...` call. Mis-dispatched `dry_run=false` is a no-op.
- Rolling-issue lifecycle (refined mid-review per user feedback):

  | Candidates | Open rolling issue exists | Action |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0 | no | Silent (`$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` only). |
  | 0 | yes, idle < 28 days | Silent. |
  | 0 | yes, idle ≥ 28 days | Auto-close with a final comment. |
  | > 0 | no | Create new rolling issue. |
  | > 0 | yes | Append a comment. |

- 2 files, 264 net insertions. Merged onto `main` as [#101](https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/101).

## What worked

- **Scope-discipline.** Plan locked to "workflow + runbook, dry-run only, no DELETE call anywhere". Landed exactly as specified. Goal C (2-week observation) and Goal D (actual deletion) explicitly deferred to follow-up PRs.
- **Mid-review tightening.** Original spec appended a "no candidates" comment every Monday — would grow the rolling issue unboundedly. User requested a lower-cost shape; one extra commit (`0865006`) refactored to: empty weeks are silent, auto-close after 4 consecutive idle weeks. The change landed before merge, not as a follow-up — kept the PR's blast radius the same.
- **Defense-in-depth on permissions.** `contents: read` plus the absence of any `DELETE` call means Goal D's review has two independent gates to flip (widen permissions **and** add the call), not just one input default.
- **§2 fact-check.** `.github/rulesets/all-branches.json` was read directly to verify the issue body's claim that non-default branch deletion isn't ruleset-blocked. The rule set has `non_fast_forward` only — deletion intentionally omitted (`docs/rulesets.md:12`). Claim confirmed before writing any code.
- **CI verification mode behaved as designed.** `verify-agents / detect` correctly classified the PR as non-APM-relevant → `verify` skipped. `verify-apm-drift / verify` triggered (workflow files changed) and passed (`apm compile` produced no drift). No regressions surfaced.

## What to watch (deferred verification from #101 test plan)

The planning environment can `git push` but cannot `gh workflow run` against the live repo. These were explicitly deferred in the PR body and must be run post-merge by the operator:

- [ ] **Empty default golden path** — `gh workflow run branch-cleanup.yml --ref main -f dry_run=true -f min_age_days=60`. Confirm: green, no rolling issue created, log ends with `Empty run, no open rolling issue. Silent.`
- [ ] **Forced-hit edge** — `gh workflow run ... -f min_age_days=0`. Confirm: rolling issue is created with the candidate table.
- [ ] **Append on second hit** — second `min_age_days=0` dispatch. Confirm: same issue gets a new comment, not a duplicate.
- [ ] **Idle close** — set `IDLE_CLOSE_DAYS: "0"` locally (do not commit) and dispatch an empty run with the test issue still open. Confirm: issue is auto-closed with the expected final comment.
- [ ] **First scheduled tick** — next Monday 05:00 JST. Should be silent unless a real orphan exists.
- [ ] **Cleanup test artifacts** — close any rolling issue opened during the forced-hit / append tests, since those dispatches will not satisfy the 28-day auto-close threshold.

## Lift into the harness

Same gap as #100: this retro was filed by operator-prompted memory (`PR merged` → agent reacts). The retro-issue-creation workflow itself is still deferred (out-of-scope of #97; tracked indirectly through #63 Phase 8 and #84 redesign). Until that lands, every merge will continue to produce a `retro: …` issue opened by the merging agent.

The branch-cleanup workflow does **not** itself qualify as "the retro harness" — different surface (it watches stale branches, not merge events). Filing a separate workflow remains the right shape.

## Out of scope for this retro

- **Goal C (#31)** — 2-week dry-run observation period. Pure operations; not a code change.
- **Goal D (#31)** — widen `permissions` to `contents: write`, add gated `gh api DELETE` call, flip `dry_run` default. Requires its own issue/PR after the observation period; must verify that Goal D's review re-checks **both** the permissions widening **and** the new DELETE call.
- **Goal D safety addition** — `apply-rulesets.yml` / `apply-labels.yml` both have a `Guard dispatch ref` step that rejects dispatch from anywhere other than `main`. `branch-cleanup.yml` does **not** — acceptable while the workflow is read-only, but Goal D must add it before merging.
- **#84 label taxonomy redesign** — the rolling issue's `layer:meta` + `type:docs` labels may need re-classification once the new taxonomy lands. Independent track.

items.original:
## Problem

The Claude Code on the Web remote environment ships a default `uv` at `0.8.17`, but this repository's `pyproject.toml` declares `required-version = ">=0.11.8"`. As a result, `uv sync --locked` fails immediately at session start, forcing a manual `uv` reinstall every time.

CI (`.github/workflows/generate-agents.yml`, `.github/workflows/verify-apm-drift.yml`) already pins `UV_VERSION: "0.11.11"` via a curl install, so CI and the remote session are out of sync.

## Approach

- **No nix.** Installing nix purely to deliver one binary adds 60–90 s to every container creation; it conflicts with CLAUDE.md §4 ("minimum code that solves the problem"). On top of that, `nixpkgs.uv` trails upstream releases by up to several days, which works *against* the goal of "always current".
- Register a curl install — the same pattern CI uses — in the **Claude Code on the Web Environment setup script** (configured outside the repo, in the Web UI). Pin `UV_VERSION` to the same `0.11.11` CI uses.
- `docs/repo-scope.md` (#58) forbids committing anything under `.claude/`, so a `SessionStart` hook is not an option. The trigger has to live outside the repo. This is a structural constraint, not a preference.

## Deliverables

- Add `docs/remote-environment.md` — a runbook covering: the setup script body, the sync rule against CI's `UV_VERSION`, the verification recipe, and the update procedure. This sits in the "operator runbooks" carve-out of `docs/repo-scope.md`.
- Outside the repo: paste the setup script into the Claude Code on the Web Environment settings (manual operator step).

## Verification

In a fresh session:

1. `uv --version` reports `uv 0.11.11`.
2. `uv sync --locked` succeeds.
3. `uv run --with "apm-cli==0.12.1" apm compile` produces no diff in `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` (matches the CI `verify-apm-drift` gate).

Sub-issue of #58. Bootstrap dependency for #106.

## Motivation

#106 needs a session-start trigger that runs **before** the user's first command in the remote environment, to pin `uv` to the CI `UV_VERSION`. The only repo-internal place that can express this is a Claude Code `SessionStart` hook in `.claude/settings.json`.

The current `docs/repo-scope.md` prohibition blocks that file. The Web-UI Environment setup script is the workaround #107 documents, but it has a structural drawback: the trigger lives outside git, so it cannot be code-reviewed, cannot be diffed against CI, and cannot be reproduced when an environment is recreated. The same supply-chain concern that motivated the broad `.claude/` ban applies to the Web UI script — and arguably more so, because the Web UI is not under change control at all.

## Proposal

Carve out **only** `.claude/settings.json` (single file, not the broader `.claude/` directory). The minimum surface needed to host a `SessionStart` hook for deterministic provisioning.

- `.gitignore` — add `!.claude/settings.json` exception under the existing `.claude/` ignore.
- `.claudeignore` — mirror exactly.
- `docs/repo-scope.md` — add a row to the "Existing carve-outs that stay valid" table, with the rationale recorded inline.
- The broader `.claude/` directory rule stays in effect — anything else under `.claude/` remains prohibited.

## Security tradeoff being accepted

This is the conscious tradeoff this issue records, per CLAUDE.md §4 ("Simplicity, **bounded by safety**").

| Risk accepted | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| A committed hook can run arbitrary shell at session start — supply-chain risk. | Hook contents are reviewed in PRs like any other code. The carve-out is one file, not a directory; nothing else can sneak in. |
| Future hook content could be tool-specific in ways that violate the repo's tool-agnostic purpose. | Reviewer enforcement, plus the content-based rule in `docs/repo-scope.md` § "Open Q1 resolution" still applies — content that exists solely for one agent tool's UX is still out of scope. |
| `.claude/settings.json` may also carry `permissions` / `model` / `apiKeyHelper` fields with their own security surface. | Same review enforcement. The carve-out is for the *file*, but the bar for what's allowed *inside* it stays "deterministic provisioning that is tool-agnostic in spirit". |

## Non-goals

- Do **not** carve out `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/commands/`, or any other subdirectory. If hook logic grows beyond what fits inline in `settings.json`, put scripts under `scripts/` (already permitted) and call them from the hook.
- Do **not** lift the broader `.claude/` ban or any other tool-specific path.
- Do **not** treat this carve-out as precedent for permitting other tools' config (`.cursor/`, `.aider*`, etc.).

## Acceptance

The PR closing this issue must:

1. Update `.gitignore`, `.claudeignore`, and `docs/repo-scope.md` together (per `docs/repo-scope.md` § Update procedure / Rollback).
2. Pass the *Verify* recipe in `docs/repo-scope.md` — `git check-ignore -v .claude/settings.json` must print a negated rule, and `git check-ignore -v .claude/anything-else` must still print the broader exclude.
3. Reference both this issue and #58 in the commit message and PR body.

**Supersedes #42** (Phase 3-B). The `commit_message_pattern: #\d+` approach proposed there does not enforce upstream-issue linkage because GitHub's auto-appended `(#)` suffix trivially satisfies the regex; see #42's closing comment for the fact-level rationale.

## Symptom (fact)

#108 was merged with `Refs #` left empty in the PR body. CLAUDE.md §3 mandates that every PR cite its issue number, but the rule is enforced only by prose in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and by reviewer attention — both of which failed silently. The missing link was caught and corrected post-merge by an operator, not by the harness.

The PR template comment claims this is guarded:

```
GitHub synthesizes the squash commit body from this PR body, so keep the
`Refs #` line below intact — it is what satisfies the
`commit_message_pattern: #\d+` rule enforced on `main` (see issue #18
Phase 3-B and .github/rulesets/main.json).
```

…but inspection of `.github/rulesets/main.json` on `main` shows **no `commit_message_pattern` rule**:

```
$ jq '.rules | map(.type)' .github/rulesets/main.json
[
  "deletion",
  "non_fast_forward",
  "required_linear_history",
  "pull_request",
  "required_status_checks"
]
```

items.original:
Follow-up from #106 / #109 / #111. Sub-issue of #58 (deterministic-first principle).

## Problem

After #111 lands, `UV_VERSION` lives in **three** places that must stay in lockstep but have no automated cross-check:

- `.github/workflows/generate-agents.yml` — `env: UV_VERSION:`
- `.github/workflows/verify-apm-drift.yml` — `env: UV_VERSION:`
- `scripts/install-uv.sh` — `UV_VERSION="…"`

Today the only enforcement is "edit all three in the same PR" plus the retrospective-issue checklist. That is operator discipline, which CLAUDE.md §3 explicitly calls out as the wrong layer ("Push deterministic work into hooks, pre-commit, and CI/CD — build the harness first if it's missing").

Beyond local drift, there is no automated upstream-follow either: when astral-sh/uv ships a new release, nothing here proposes the bump. The "current" value can stale silently.

## Proposal: three layers stitched together

### 1. Single source of truth — `pyproject.toml`

Change `[tool.uv].required-version` from `>=0.11.8` to `==0.11.11` (or the current pinned value). PEP440 `==` makes it an exact pin; `required-version` is already uv's documented field for this.

This deletes the three duplicates in favor of one canonical value.

> **Tradeoff acknowledged.** `required-version` historically signals "minimum acceptable", not "exact pin". For this repo it is fine — we are not a library consumed downstream for its uv constraint; submodule consumers do not inherit our uv pin. The strict semantic is the desired one here.

### 2. Readers consume the single source

- **CI workflows.** Replace the manual `curl` install with `astral-sh/setup-uv@v6` configured with `version-file: pyproject.toml`. The action reads `[tool.uv].required-version` natively. This also gets cache support for free.
- **`scripts/install-uv.sh`.** Read the same field with a small `python3 -c "import tomllib; …"` (Python 3.11+ has `tomllib` in stdlib; the remote env ships 3.11+).

After this, no file outside `pyproject.toml` carries the version literal.

### 3. CI drift gate

Add a tiny lint job (new workflow or new step in `verify-agents.yml`) that:

1. Reads the pin from `pyproject.toml`.
2. Greps the rest of the tree for any version-shaped literal in workflow or script files (`grep -rE '0\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' .github/ scripts/`).
3. Fails if a literal that looks like a uv version appears anywhere other than `pyproject.toml`.

Belt-and-suspenders: catches future regressions where someone re-introduces a hardcoded copy.

### 4. Automated upstream follow — Renovate

Renovate has native uv ecosystem support. Configure it to:

- Watch `[tool.uv].required-version` in `pyproject.toml`.
- Open a PR per upstream uv release, bumping the pin.
- The drift gate in step 3 ensures the bump applies everywhere on its own (because there is only one place to bump).

(Dependabot also has uv support now, so this could be Dependabot instead — operator preference.)

## Implementation outline (one PR closes this issue)

1. `pyproject.toml`: switch `required-version` to `==0.11.11`.
2. `.github/workflows/generate-agents.yml` & `verify-apm-drift.yml`: replace the manual `Install uv` step with `astral-sh/setup-uv@v6` using `version-file: pyproject.toml`. Remove `env: UV_VERSION:` blocks.
3. `scripts/install-uv.sh`: replace the hardcoded `UV_VERSION="…"` with a TOML read of the same field.
4. Add the drift-gate lint (new workflow or step).
5. Add Renovate config (`.github/renovate.json` or `renovate.json5`) limited to uv.
6. Update `docs/remote-environment.md` and `docs/repo-scope.md` to reflect the new single source and remove the "future improvement" note that this issue closes.

## Acceptance

- No `UV_VERSION` literal exists outside `pyproject.toml` (verified by the drift-gate lint).
- Bumping `pyproject.toml` propagates to CI and the session hook with no other edits.
- Renovate opens an auto-bump PR for a contrived new upstream release (or at least the config validates against the renovate config schema).
- The verification recipe in `docs/remote-environment.md` continues to pass end-to-end.

## Risks

- **`required-version = "==X"` is unusual.** Most uv projects use it as a lower bound. Reviewers reading our `pyproject.toml` may misread it. Mitigation: an inline comment in `pyproject.toml` and the rationale in `docs/remote-environment.md`.
- **`astral-sh/setup-uv` adds a third-party action dependency.** Pin to a SHA and review action source on each bump. Alternative: keep the manual curl but read the version from `pyproject.toml` via the inline python — same single-source effect, no new action.
- **Renovate noise.** uv releases roughly weekly. If this becomes noisy, schedule batched bumps (e.g. weekly group) via Renovate config.

## Non-goals

- Do not move the `UV_VERSION` literal to a *new* file (e.g. `.uv-version`). `pyproject.toml` already exists and is the standard home for the field.
- Do not address `apm-cli` version pinning here — that is a separate concern (currently `APM_CLI_VERSION="0.12.1"` only in workflows; if it spreads, a separate issue should cover it).

items.original:
Retrospective for **#111** (merged 2026-05-21). Closes #109 (governance carve-out); bootstrap for #106 (uv pin at session start).

## What landed

- `.gitignore` / `.claudeignore`: switched `.claude/` → `.claude/*` plus `!.claude/settings.json` negation. The single-file carve-out is the narrowest possible relaxation of the #58 prohibition.
- `docs/repo-scope.md`: added the carve-out row and an inline "Security tradeoff for `.claude/settings.json`" section recording the accepted risk.
- `.claude/settings.json`: registers `scripts/install-uv.sh` as the `SessionStart` hook.
- `scripts/install-uv.sh`: idempotent, `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE`-guarded, pins `uv` to `0.11.11` matching CI.
- `docs/remote-environment.md`: rewritten from the Web-UI-based draft (#107) to a hook-based runbook; closing note points UV_VERSION drift to #112.

## What went well

- **Plan-mode-first paid off.** The `AskUserQuestion` round (carve-out scope / rollout / Web UI fate) eliminated rework — there was zero churn on scope decisions once the plan was approved.
- **Test recipe caught a real bug pre-commit.** The first attempt used `.claude/` + `!.claude/settings.json`; `git check-ignore -v` immediately showed the negation was inert because the parent dir was excluded. Switched to `.claude/*` and re-verified with a positive (`git add settings.json` works) and three negative (`settings.local.json` / `hooks/install.sh` / arbitrary file blocked) tests.
- **Subagent split discipline held.** Explore-only agents read; the implementation happened in the main loop; verification stayed in-loop too. No "agent reviews own work" violation.
- **Drift surface flagged during review** and tracked at #112 with a concrete 3-point bundle instead of a vague "future improvement" pointer. The runbook was updated in-PR to cite #112.

## What did not go well

- **PR stacking mis-merged.** #111's base was `claude/update-uv-nix-x47W4` (the #107 branch), expecting GitHub to auto-retarget once #107 merged. Instead, #111 was merged *first*, into #107's branch — so the work is now on the #107 branch waiting for that PR to merge into `main`. The cost is one extra merge step and that #107's body still describes the now-superseded Web-UI approach. Lesson: stacked PRs need an explicit "merge order" note in both PRs' bodies, not just one.
- **#107's body went stale.** The Web-UI runbook PR body was never updated to reflect that #111 replaced its content. A reviewer reading #107's title and body today would expect Web-UI content, not the hook-based runbook actually on the branch. Should have been an in-PR edit when #111 landed.
- **Three-file `UV_VERSION` duplication shipped.** Required reviewer to catch it and motivate #112. The deterministic-first principle would have suggested designing the single-source layer *before* writing the hook — but the carve-out PR was already in flight. Pragmatic, but the lesson is to plan provisioning + drift control together next time.
- **`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` is set in the parent shell**, so the first "no-op outside remote env" test passed for the wrong reason. Caught it only by adding `env -u CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE`. Lesson: when testing guards, explicitly unset the variable, do not assume the test shell is clean.

## Action items

- [ ] **Update PR #107's body** to reflect that the branch now carries the hook-based rollup, not the Web-UI draft. Edit the title too if appropriate.
- [ ] **Merge #107** to land the full bundle on `main`.
- [ ] **Address #112** (single-source `UV_VERSION` in `pyproject.toml`, CI drift gate, Renovate auto-bump) as the next layer.
- [ ] **Convention for stacked PRs** — add a short paragraph to `CLAUDE.md` §3 or `docs/rulesets.md` describing the "stacked PR merge order" expectation and the body-update obligation when the lower PR's content is replaced.

## Links

- PR: https://github.com/tvna/claude-md/pull/111
- Governance issue closed: #109
- Bootstrap target: #106
- Follow-up tracked: #112
- Parent: #58

## Symptom (fact)

#117 added `{"context": "Verify issue link / gate"}` to `.github/rulesets/main.json` (SoT) and merged. The live `main-protection` ruleset on GitHub does **not** yet include that context — and will not until `apply-rulesets.yml` is dispatched. During that lag window:

- `verify-issue-link.yml` runs on every PR, but its `Verify issue link / gate` job is **not enforced as required** on live `main` — only declared as required in the SoT JSON.
- Any PR can merge with the new gate red as long as no reviewer notices.

#30 / `.github/workflows/ruleset-drift.yml` (delivered by #116) detects this drift, but only on its **weekly cron** (Mon 06:00 JST) plus manual `workflow_dispatch`. Up to ~7 days of bleed before the operator is alerted.

## Root cause (fact)

Two design gaps that #30 intentionally does not cover:

1. **No PR-time sync check.** Every PR sees only the SoT perspective. Nothing examines whether the live ruleset already contains the contexts that the SoT now claims are required. Drift can stack across multiple PRs (SoT adds context A in PR #N, context B in PR #N+1, both unapplied) and lingers until next Monday.
2. **#30 is async by design.** It is a weekly cron + manual dispatch detector that opens issues *after* drift exists; it does not block forward motion.

CLAUDE.md §3: "Push deterministic work into hooks, pre-commit, and CI/CD." Closing the lag window mechanically (vs. operator memory) is in scope.

## Scope of fix

Narrow scope per the requesting interpretation — focus on `required_status_checks` lag, **not** full ruleset drift (#30 already owns that).

1. **Add `.github/workflows/verify-ruleset-sync.yml`** triggered on `pull_request` (all paths, not gated by `paths:` — so previous unsynced PRs are also caught by every subsequent PR). Permissions: `contents: read`. Uses the same `RULESETS_PAT` secret as `ruleset-drift.yml`.

2. **Steps:**
   - Fetch live `main-protection` ruleset via `GET /repos/${REPO}/rulesets/${id}`.
   - Read PR-**base** SoT (`.github/rulesets/main.json` from `github.base_ref`, **not** PR HEAD). This sidesteps the chicken-and-egg where a PR introducing a new context would otherwise self-fail.
   - Extract `.rules[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks") | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context` from each side.
   - **Fail** if the live set is missing any context present in base-ref SoT (= prior unapplied change still pending).
   - **Pass** if symmetric (= no pending dispatch debt).
   - Emit `::error::` lines listing the missing contexts and link to `docs/rulesets.md` Apply procedure.

3. **Promote to required status check** by adding `{"context": "Verify ruleset sync / gate"}` to `.github/rulesets/main.json` → `required_status_checks`. After merge + dispatch of this issue's PR, the gate becomes required and any unapplied SoT change blocks subsequent PRs until `apply-rulesets.yml` is dispatched.

## Out of scope

- **Post-merge auto-apply** (Option B in the design menu) — separate concern with its own risks around silent live writes; file separately if wanted.
- **Dead-context detection** (Option C) — verifying that each SoT context corresponds to an actual workflow output; orthogonal axis.
- **Full-field SoT-vs-live drift** — already covered by #30 / `ruleset-drift.yml`.
- **`all-branches.json` sync** — currently no `required_status_checks` there, so a lag is vacuous; revisit only if a future change introduces required checks there.
- **Forcing pre-merge dispatch** — the base-ref read above sidesteps this. We accept that the first PR introducing a new context still leaves a lag until dispatch; this gate ensures the lag is exactly **one PR window**, not weekly.

## Open design questions (per §2)

- **Q1 — `pull_request` vs `pull_request_target`?** `pull_request_target` runs with base-branch permissions and can read secrets even on fork PRs, but is also higher-risk. This repo is single-author and `RULESETS_PAT` is sensitive; `pull_request` is sufficient. Confirm before implementation.
- **Q2 — How to read base-ref SoT?** Two options:
  - (a) `git fetch origin ${base_ref} && git show origin/${base_ref}:.github/rulesets/main.json` — requires checkout, costs ~5 s.
  - (b) `gh api /repos/${REPO}/contents/.github/rulesets/main.json?ref=${base_ref}` (decode base64) — no checkout. Recommended.
- **Q3 — What if live is *ahead* of SoT (live has contexts not in SoT)?** That is full ruleset drift territory and #30 already files an issue. This workflow should not duplicate; it only checks the "live lagging behind SoT" direction.
- **Q4 — Strictness on the first PR after this issue lands?** If `main` already has stale unapplied SoT (e.g., #117 not yet dispatched at that moment), THIS PR would self-fail. Resolution: dispatch `apply-rulesets.yml` *before* opening the implementation PR so live is in sync with current `main` SoT.

## Verify

After the fix lands:

```sh
# 1. Workflow exists
test -f .github/workflows/verify-ruleset-sync.yml

# 2. Required status check declared in SoT
jq '.rules[] | select(.type=="required_status_checks") | .parameters.required_status_checks[].context' \
  .github/rulesets/main.json
# must include "Verify ruleset sync / gate"

# 3. Negative test: with live ruleset still missing "Verify issue link / gate"
#    (i.e., #117's context not yet applied), open a draft PR → gate fails
#    with explicit listing of the missing contexts.

# 4. Positive test: dispatch `apply-rulesets.yml` with dry_run=false →
#    next PR's gate passes.

# 5. Persistence: with live in sync, open another PR that ADDS a new context
#    to SoT — gate PASSES (because it checks base-ref SoT, not PR HEAD).
#    After that PR merges and BEFORE the next dispatch, every new PR's gate
#    FAILS until dispatch runs.
```

## Refs

- Trigger example: #117 (`Verify issue link / gate` not yet in live as of merge).
- Sibling / partial overlap: #30 (closed; weekly cron, full-field diff).
- Async detector implementation: #116 (`ruleset-drift.yml`).
- Apply pipeline: `.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml`.
- SoT: `.github/rulesets/main.json`.
- Runbook: `docs/rulesets.md`.
- CLAUDE.md §3 — "Push deterministic work into hooks, pre-commit, and CI/CD."

This is `type:feat` + `layer:p3-harness` + `layer:meta` — a deterministic PR-time gate around the ruleset apply pipeline, not a CLAUDE.md principle change.

items.original:
Follow-up from #112 / #118. Sub-issue of #58 (deterministic-first principle, "build the harness first").

## Problem

#118 landed the uv pin consolidation: `pyproject.toml` `[tool.uv].required-version` is the single source of truth, and three workflows + `scripts/install-uv.sh` read it via inline Python. The drift gate lives as inline `bash` + `grep` inside `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`.

That works, but it means the **pin-reading and drift-checking logic is only exercised by CI itself**. There are no unit tests; bugs in the regex (e.g. false-positives on `APM_CLI_VERSION`, or missing the single-quoted-literal edge case) are only caught when they actually break CI on a real PR. The same Python snippet is copy-pasted into four call sites, so a fix has to be propagated four times.

CLAUDE.md §3 says "Push deterministic work into hooks, pre-commit, and CI/CD" and "Build the harness first if it's missing". Inline duplicated logic, untestable except via end-to-end CI runs, is exactly the layer the principle warns against.

## Proposal (work already prepared on `claude/uv-pin-pytest-refactor`)

Extract the three operations into one importable Python module with a CLI:

- `scripts/uv_pin.py`
  - `read_pin(path)` — parses `[tool.uv].required-version`, validates `==X.Y.Z` shape, returns stripped pin. Raises `ValueError` with descriptive messages on every failure mode (file missing, malformed TOML, missing section, missing key, non-string, wrong specifier).
  - `find_drift(root, pin)` — runs three checks (literal-value, `UV_VERSION:` literal assignment in workflow YAML, `UV_VERSION` symbol in `docs/`); returns a list of error messages.
  - `fetch_latest_uv_release()` — wraps `gh release view`; returns `None` on any failure so callers can treat it as "skip".
  - CLI: `read` / `drift` / `stale` subcommands. Stale emits `::warning::` annotations and never fails; drift exits 1 on any finding.

- `tests/test_uv_pin.py`
  - 36 pytest cases covering: PEP440 spec validation, missing/malformed pyproject.toml handling, all three drift checks, false-positive defence (`APM_CLI_VERSION="0.12.1"`, action SHA-pin comments like `# v5.0.1`, step-env sourced from `${{ ... }}`), single-quoted-literal detection, bare-literal detection, gh subprocess failure modes (FileNotFoundError, CalledProcessError, TimeoutExpired, empty output), and CLI smoke tests.
  - One real-repo integration test calls `find_drift(REPO_ROOT, pin)` so the suite catches drift on the actual checkout — the same guarantee the CI step provides.

- Call sites delegate to the script:
  - `.github/workflows/generate-agents.yml` / `verify-apm-drift.yml` — `Read uv pin from pyproject.toml` step becomes `PIN="$(python3 scripts/uv_pin.py read)"`.
  - `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml` `lint-uv-pin` job — replaces the inline `grep` cascade with `python3 scripts/uv_pin.py drift` and `python3 scripts/uv_pin.py stale`. Adds a `Run uv_pin.py unit tests` step before the drift call, so the linter itself is gated by its own tests.
  - `scripts/install-uv.sh` — `UV_VERSION="$(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/uv_pin.py" read "$PYPROJECT")"`.

- `pyproject.toml`:
  - `[dependency-groups] dev = ["pytest>=8,<9"]` — declarative dev dep for local `uv sync --group dev`.
  - `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["scripts"]` + `testpaths = ["tests"]`.

## Acceptance

- All call sites of the inline `tomllib` snippet are removed; logic lives in one module.
- `pytest tests/` exits 0 on the real repo.
- `scripts/uv_pin.py drift` exits 0 on the real repo (current `lint-uv-pin` job behaviour preserved).
- A re-introduced `UV_VERSION: "x.y.z"` literal in any workflow yaml is caught by the unit tests *and* the CI drift step.
- No behaviour change for the SoT pin in `pyproject.toml`; the drift gate's accept/reject semantics are preserved (and now actually false-positive-tested).

## Non-goals

- Do not address `APM_CLI_VERSION` pinning (still hardcoded in workflows — separate concern, same as #112's non-goal).
- Do not switch CI install to `astral-sh/setup-uv` (the explicit choice in #112 was to keep manual `curl`).
- Do not change Dependabot or the upstream-staleness warning behaviour.

## PR

A PR will be opened directly from `claude/uv-pin-pytest-refactor`, which is already rebased onto `main` post-#118-merge. The single commit on that branch is the entire deliverable.

  - `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["scripts"]` + `testpaths = ["tests"]`.

## Acceptance

- All call sites of the inline `tomllib` snippet are removed; logic lives in one module.
- `pytest tests/` exits 0 on the real repo.
- `scripts/uv_pin.py drift` exits 0 on the real repo (current `lint-uv-pin` job behaviour preserved).
- A re-introduced `UV_VERSION: "x.y.z"` literal in any workflow yaml is caught by the unit tests *and* the CI drift step.
- No behaviour change for the SoT pin in `pyproject.toml`; the drift gate's accept/reject semantics are preserved (and now actually false-positive-tested).

## Non-goals

- Do not address `APM_CLI_VERSION` pinning (still hardcoded in workflows -- separate concern, same as #112's non-goal).
- Do not switch CI install to `astral-sh/setup-uv` (the explicit choice in #112 was to keep manual `curl`).
- Do not change Dependabot or the upstream-staleness warning behaviour.

## PR

A PR will be opened directly from `claude/uv-pin-pytest-refactor`, which is already rebased onto `main` post-#118-merge. The single commit on that branch is the entire deliverable.

## Context

#112 (closed by #118 + #122) consolidated `UV_VERSION` into `pyproject.toml`, extracted CI's inline bash into `scripts/uv_pin.py`, and added 36 pytest cases (`tests/test_uv_pin.py`) to lock down behaviour. The `lint-uv-pin` drift gate now exercises that logic on every PR. That work proved a reusable pattern:

> When a CI workflow carries non-trivial inline shell logic, extract the logic into a pure(-ish) Python module under `scripts/`, cover it with pytest under `tests/`, and have the workflow shell out to the Python entry point.

CLAUDE.md §3: "Push deterministic work into hooks, pre-commit, and CI/CD - build the harness first if it's missing." Inline YAML bash is the *opposite* of deterministic — it cannot be unit-tested, refactored safely, or exercised offline. The same pattern that worked for `uv_pin.py` should be applied to the remaining five workflows that still carry sizable inline shell.

## Workflows in scope (fact)

| Workflow | Inline LOC (est.) | Hardcoded logic |
|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml` | ~30 | HTML-comment stripping, `Refs|Closes|Fixes|Resolves` regex extraction, per-ref existence check |
| `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` | ~180 | input validation, branch age math, candidate filtering, rolling-issue lifecycle (create / append / idle-close) |
| `.github/workflows/ruleset-drift.yml` | ~190 | per-ruleset SoT vs live diff, unknown-on-live set difference, two distinct issue-body generators |
| `.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml` | ~170 | ruleset SoT vs live diff, POST/PUT decision, HTTP retry with backoff, auto-delete-branch toggle |
| `.github/workflows/apply-labels.yml` | ~160 | label SoT vs live diff, POST/PATCH/DELETE with retry, step-summary table generation |

Combined: **~730 lines of currently-untestable shell.**

## Scope of fix

Each workflow gets its own sub-issue and its own PR. The shape of each sub-PR mirrors #122:

1. Pure logic moves to `scripts/.py` exposing testable functions + an argparse CLI.
2. Side-effecting wrappers (GitHub REST API client, `gh` invocations, file I/O) sit at the module boundary and are mocked in tests (`monkeypatch`, `subprocess.run` stubs).
3. `tests/test_.py` covers: happy path, every error branch (loud failure per §4), every CLI flag, false-positive defences specific to that workflow.
4. The YAML workflow shells out to the Python entry point with no inline logic beyond `python3 scripts/.py  [args]`.
5. `verify-agents.yml` runs the new pytest module on every PR (extend the existing `lint-uv-pin` job, or split off a sibling `lint-scripts` job once a second test module lands - rule of three).

### Reused infrastructure already in place from #112

- `[dependency-groups] dev = ["pytest>=8,<9"]` in `pyproject.toml`
- `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["scripts"]` and `testpaths = ["tests"]`
- CI pattern: `pip install --user 'pytest>=8,<9'` + `python3 -m pytest -v`
- `scripts/uv_pin.py`'s subprocess-mocking pattern for `gh release view`

## Sub-issue checklist (filed under this tracking issue)

Priority order — **smallest to largest, read-only before mutating**, to iterate the testing pattern safely:

- [ ] **1.** `verify-issue-link.yml` -> `scripts/issue_link.py` + `tests/test_issue_link.py` *(~30 LOC, pure regex + 1 API call, lowest blast radius)*
- [ ] **2.** `branch-cleanup.yml` -> `scripts/branch_cleanup.py` + `tests/test_branch_cleanup.py` *(read-only survey; no destructive code path exists)*
- [ ] **3.** `ruleset-drift.yml` -> `scripts/ruleset_drift.py` + `tests/test_ruleset_drift.py` *(read-only detection; opens issues only)*
- [ ] **4.** `apply-rulesets.yml` -> `scripts/rulesets_apply.py` + `tests/test_rulesets_apply.py` *(mutating; gated by `environment: ruleset-apply`)*
- [ ] **5.** `apply-labels.yml` -> `scripts/labels_apply.py` + `tests/test_labels_apply.py` *(mutating + the densest reconciliation logic)*

## Out of scope

- Replacing the workflows themselves with composite actions / reusable workflows (different concern).
- Changing the **behaviour** of any workflow - this is a pure refactor. Same outputs, same `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` contents, same exit codes.
- Adding new feature gates or new workflows (e.g. #120 is orthogonal).
- Migrating from `gh` CLI / `curl` to a third-party Python GitHub SDK (`PyGithub`, `githubkit`). Stdlib + subprocess keeps zero new wheels - revisit only if a sub-issue's tests outgrow that.
- `generate-agents.yml` and `verify-apm-drift.yml` - already touched by #112 and now carry minimal inline logic. Leave them.

## Acceptance (umbrella completion)

- [ ] All 5 sub-issues closed via their own PRs.
- [ ] Inline shell per workflow drops to <20 LOC of bash (target: just the `python3 scripts/.py` invocation + any required env-var marshalling).
- [ ] `tests/test_*.py` modules cover every extracted function; CI runs all of them on every PR.
- [ ] Workflow behaviour preserved — verified by re-running each in `dry_run=true` / `mode=verify` against `main` after each sub-PR merges.
- [ ] Retrospective issue auto-opened (or filed manually per CLAUDE.md §3) after the last sub-PR merges.

## Risks

- **Mutating workflows (`apply-labels`, `apply-rulesets`).** Refactoring code that performs live API writes is higher blast-radius than the read-only ones. Mitigation: do them last (per priority above); exercise each refactored workflow with `dry_run=true` first.
- **Test isolation for `gh` / `curl` subprocess calls.** `scripts/uv_pin.py`'s `fetch_latest_uv_release()` already established the pattern: wrap in a function, monkeypatch `subprocess.run`. Reuse rather than reinvent.
- **HTTP retry duplication.** `apply-labels.yml` and `apply-rulesets.yml` both hand-roll a 3-attempt retry with exponential backoff. Consider extracting into a shared `scripts/_github_api.py` only after the **third** sub-issue confirms duplication (CLAUDE.md §4 — rule of three). Until then, copy-paste is correct.

## References

- Precedent (the refactor pattern this issue applies elsewhere): #112 -> PR #118 + PR #122.
- Reusable scaffolding: `scripts/uv_pin.py`, `tests/test_uv_pin.py`, `[dependency-groups]` in `pyproject.toml`.
- Origin issues for each workflow being refactored: #110 (`verify-issue-link`), #31 (`branch-cleanup`), #30 (`ruleset-drift`), #18 (`apply-rulesets`, `apply-labels`).
- Sibling open harness issues (orthogonal, not blocked by this): #120, #110, #102.
- Label taxonomy: #84.
- CLAUDE.md §3 — deterministic gates; §4 — fail loudly, no silent defaults.

items.original:
Sub-issue of #123 (priority 1 of 5 — smallest, lowest blast radius). Mirrors the pattern proved by #112 -> #122.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml` (originated by #110) carries ~30 lines of inline bash that:

1. Strips `` from the PR body via `perl -0777 -pe 's///gs'`.
2. Extracts every `Refs|Closes|Fixes|Resolves #` reference via `grep -Eio`, deduplicates via `sort -u`.
3. Calls `gh api /repos/${REPO}/issues/${n}` once per extracted ref to verify existence.
4. Emits `::error::` annotations for missing/non-existent refs.

This is the gate enforcing CLAUDE.md §3 ("cite the issue number in every PR"). It is presently untestable — comment-stripping, the regex alternation, and the existence-check branching cannot be asserted without dispatching a real workflow run.

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/issue_link.py` (new)

Pure functions:
- `strip_html_comments(body: str) -> str` — drops `` including newlines.
- `extract_refs(body: str) -> list[int]` — deduplicated, sorted list of issue numbers matched by `^[ \t]*(Refs|Closes|Fixes|Resolves)[ \t]+#(\d+)\b` (case-insensitive, multi-line).
- `verify_ref_exists(repo: str, number: int, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> bool` — wraps `gh api /repos/{repo}/issues/{number} --silent`; runner is overridable for tests.

CLI:
- `python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo OWNER/NAME --body-file PATH` — reads body from file (workflow writes `$PR_BODY` to a temp file first), runs the three steps, prints `::error::` on failure, exits non-zero if (a) zero refs or (b) any ref does not resolve.

### `tests/test_issue_link.py` (new, target: ~25 cases)

- `TestStripHtmlComments` — empty body, no comment, single-line comment, multi-line comment, multiple comments, nested-looking text (``), comment containing newlines, comment containing `Refs #1` (must be stripped before extraction).
- `TestExtractRefs` — one each of `Refs`/`Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves`, case-insensitivity, leading-whitespace tolerated, deduplication, sorted output, ignores `See #N` / `cf #N` / bare `#N`, ignores refs that were inside comments (after stripping), handles `\r\n` line endings.
- `TestVerifyRefExists` — success (rc=0), missing (non-zero rc), gh missing (FileNotFoundError), all monkeypatched.
- `TestCLI` — empty body fails with documented error; single valid ref passes; multiple valid refs pass; ref to non-existent issue fails with `::error::`; mix of valid+invalid fails listing only the invalid.

### `.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml`

Replace the ~30-line shell block with: write `$PR_BODY` to `/tmp/pr-body`, run `python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo "${REPO}" --body-file /tmp/pr-body`. Permissions and event types unchanged.

### `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`

`lint-uv-pin` job gains a step: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_issue_link.py -v`. Decide whether to rename the job to `lint-scripts` only after a second sub-issue lands (rule of three).

## Out of scope

- Adding new validation rules (e.g. reject closed-only refs, enforce single-Closes, reject cross-repo refs). Behaviour is preserved exactly.
- Replacing `gh api` with the GitHub MCP SDK or `httpx`. Stays subprocess.

## Verify

- `uv run --group dev pytest tests/test_issue_link.py -v` passes locally.
- Draft PR with empty `Refs #` -> gate fails with the documented error.
- Draft PR with `Refs #99999999` -> gate fails with "Referenced #99999999 does not exist".
- Draft PR with `Refs #` -> gate passes.
- Diff the new YAML against the old: the only inline logic left is the temp-file write + the Python invocation.

## Refs

- Parent tracking: #123
- Pattern precedent: #112 -> PR #118 + PR #122; `scripts/uv_pin.py` / `tests/test_uv_pin.py`.
- Workflow origin: #110.
- CLAUDE.md §3 (issue-link enforcement), §4 (fail loudly, no silent skips).

Sub-issue of #123 (priority 2 of 5 — read-only survey, no destructive code path exists yet). Mirrors the pattern proved by #112 -> #122.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` (originated by #31, see retro #104) carries ~180 lines of inline bash across two steps (`Survey candidate branches`, `Maintain rolling summary issue`) that:

1. Validate `dry_run` (boolean) and `min_age_days` (non-negative integer) inputs.
2. Walk every branch from `gh api --paginate /repos/${REPO}/branches`, parse last-commit dates, compute age in days, filter out (a) the default branch, (b) anything newer than `min_age_days`, (c) anything with an open PR.
3. Write rows to both `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and `/tmp/cleanup-comment.md`.
4. Reconcile against a rolling summary issue: create if missing-and-candidates>0; append comment if exists-and-candidates>0; auto-close if existing-but-idle ≥ 28 days; silent otherwise.

The candidate-filter algebra and the 5-row state table of the rolling-issue lifecycle (#104's table) are the kind of logic that pytest excels at — but right now they live as `gh` shell-outs and `date -u -d ... +%s` arithmetic that can only be smoke-tested in CI.

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/branch_cleanup.py` (new)

Pure functions (no I/O):
- `parse_dry_run(raw: str) -> bool` — accepts `"true"`/`"false"`, raises `ValueError` otherwise.
- `parse_min_age_days(raw: str) -> int` — non-negative integer, raises `ValueError` otherwise.
- `is_candidate(*, branch: str, default_branch: str, last_commit_utc: datetime, now_utc: datetime, min_age_days: int, has_open_pr: bool) -> bool` — the four-condition filter.
- `format_summary_row(branch: str, last_commit_utc: datetime, age_days: int, sha: str) -> str` — Markdown table row.
- `decide_issue_action(*, candidate_count: int, existing_issue: dict | None, idle_seconds: int, idle_threshold_seconds: int) -> Literal["create", "append", "close", "silent"]` — the 5-row state table from #104.

Side-effect wrappers (mockable):
- `list_branches(repo: str, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> list[tuple[str, str]]` — `gh api --paginate /repos/.../branches`.
- `get_last_commit_date(repo: str, sha: str, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> datetime`.
- `count_open_prs_for_head(repo: str, branch: str, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> int`.
- `find_rolling_issue(repo: str, title: str, *, runner=subprocess.run) -> dict | None`.
- `comment_on_issue(...)`, `create_issue(...)`, `close_issue_with_comment(...)`.

CLI:
- `python3 scripts/branch_cleanup.py survey --repo OWNER/NAME --dry-run BOOL --min-age-days N --default-branch BRANCH` — writes summary table to stdout, writes per-row comment file to `--out PATH`, prints candidate count to stderr.
- `python3 scripts/branch_cleanup.py reconcile --repo OWNER/NAME --title TITLE --candidate-count N --comment-file PATH --idle-close-days 28` — implements the 5-row state machine.

### `tests/test_branch_cleanup.py` (new, target: ~35 cases)

- `TestParseDryRun` / `TestParseMinAgeDays` — happy + every reject case.
- `TestIsCandidate` — default-branch excluded; age below threshold excluded; open-PR excluded; all-clear included; boundary at exactly `min_age_days` (the existing `>` semantic must be preserved).
- `TestFormatSummaryRow` — SHA truncation to 7 chars, ISO date pass-through.
- `TestDecideIssueAction` — every cell of the 5-row state table from #104, plus the boundary at exactly 28 days.
- `TestListBranches` — pagination handling (mock 2 pages), empty repo (no branches), single branch.
- `TestGetLastCommitDate` — parses GitHub's ISO-8601 with `Z` suffix; `+00:00` form; raises on malformed.
- `TestCountOpenPrsForHead` — 0, 1, many.
- `TestCLI survey` — empty repo prints `Total branches: 0`, candidate_count=0; single old orphan listed; old branch with open PR excluded.
- `TestCLI reconcile` — every state-machine outcome end-to-end with monkeypatched gh stubs.

### `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml`

Both inline shell steps collapse to single Python invocations. Idle-close threshold stays as `IDLE_CLOSE_DAYS: "28"` env var (passed through `--idle-close-days`).

### `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`

`lint-uv-pin` (or its successor `lint-scripts` once we hit rule of three) gains a step running this module's pytest.

Sub-issue of #123 (priority 3 of 5 — read-only detection; opens issues only, no live writes). Mirrors the pattern proved by #112 -> #122.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/ruleset-drift.yml` (originated by #30, delivered by #116) carries ~190 lines of inline bash across `Diff SoT vs live and detect unknown rulesets` + two `gh issue create` steps that:

1. Walk every SoT file in `.github/rulesets/*.json`; for each, fetch the matching live ruleset via `GET /repos/.../rulesets/{id}` and `diff -u` the canonical projection (`{name, target, enforcement, conditions, bypass_actors, rules}`).
2. Classify each into `in-sync` / `missing-on-live` / `drift` / `ambiguous` (multiple live rulesets with the same name -> abort).
3. Detect "unknown" rulesets (live name not present in SoT name set) via jq set difference.
4. Emit two structured issue bodies — one for SoT-vs-live drift, one for unknown rulesets — each with summary table, per-ruleset diff blocks, and a remediation section.
5. File issues only when the corresponding count > 0, with specific labels (`layer:meta` + `type:fix`).

The classification logic and the issue-body composition are pure transformations of JSON inputs to Markdown outputs. They cannot be unit-tested today; the only signal is whether a real cron run produces a sensible issue.

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/ruleset_drift.py` (new)

Pure functions:
- `classify(sot: dict, live_rulesets: list[dict]) -> dict` — returns `{"status": "in-sync"|"missing-on-live"|"drift"|"ambiguous", "live_id": int|None, "match_count": int}` for one SoT entry.
- `canonical_projection(ruleset: dict) -> dict` — returns the comparable subset `{name, target, enforcement, conditions, bypass_actors, rules}` sorted.
- `diff_canonical(sot: dict, live: dict) -> str` — unified-diff string (delegates to `difflib.unified_diff`, since stdlib gives byte-equivalent output to `diff -u`).
- `find_unknown(sot_names: list[str], live: list[dict]) -> list[dict]` — set difference returning `{id, name, target, enforcement}` tuples.
- `render_sot_drift_issue(*, run_url: str, run_date: str, repo: str, rows: list[dict], diffs: list[tuple[str, int, str]]) -> str` — full Markdown body.
- `render_unknown_issue(*, run_url: str, run_date: str, unknowns: list[dict]) -> str` — full Markdown body.
- `render_summary_section(rows: list[dict], header: str) -> str` — shared Markdown table renderer for `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.

Side-effect wrappers (mockable):
- `fetch_live_rulesets_list(repo: str, token: str, *, opener=urllib.request.urlopen) -> list[dict]` — `GET /repos/.../rulesets`.
- `fetch_live_ruleset(repo: str, ruleset_id: int, token: str, *, opener=...) -> dict`.
- `file_issue(repo: str, title: str, body_file: Path, labels: list[str], *, runner=subprocess.run) -> None`.

CLI:
- `python3 scripts/ruleset_drift.py detect --repo OWNER/NAME --sot-dir .github/rulesets --run-url URL --summary-file PATH --sot-body-file PATH --unknown-body-file PATH` — does the read + classify + render, writes summary + issue bodies to the named files, prints `drift_count` and `unknown_count` to stdout (for `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`).
- `python3 scripts/ruleset_drift.py file-sot-issue --repo OWNER/NAME --run-date YYYY-MM-DD --body-file PATH` — `gh issue create` wrapper.
- `python3 scripts/ruleset_drift.py file-unknown-issue --repo OWNER/NAME --run-date YYYY-MM-DD --body-file PATH` — ditto.

### `tests/test_ruleset_drift.py` (new, target: ~40 cases)

- `TestClassify` — in-sync, missing-on-live, drift (one field differs), drift (rules differ in order — must still drift), ambiguous (2 matches).
- `TestCanonicalProjection` — only the 6 fields kept; sort-stability across rules list; ignores live-only metadata (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, etc.).
- `TestDiffCanonical` — empty diff returns empty string; field-rename produces +/- pair; rules-list reorder shows up as diff (which is the intended behaviour today).
- `TestFindUnknown` — empty live, all-known, single unknown, multiple unknowns, names with special chars (URL-encode-safe).
- `TestRenderSotDriftIssue` — header includes `Parent: #30`, run URL, RUN_DATE; table has correct columns; `Diffs` section appears only when ≥1 drift row; `Remediation` section literal preserved.
- `TestRenderUnknownIssue` — header includes `Parent: #30`; "Unknown rulesets" table; remediation links to `docs/rulesets.md` rollback section.
- `TestFetchLiveRulesetsList` — happy path; auth header included; 401 raises with descriptive message.
- `TestFetchLiveRuleset` — same.
- `TestFileIssue` — labels passed through; body-file existence asserted; subprocess args validated.
- `TestCLI detect` — clean tree (drift=0, unknown=0); SoT drift only; unknown only; both; ambiguous live causes non-zero exit.

### `.github/workflows/ruleset-drift.yml`

Three inline shell steps collapse to three Python invocations. `RULESETS_PAT` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` env vars unchanged.

### `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`

`lint-uv-pin` job (likely renamed to `lint-scripts` by this point — third sub-issue passes the rule of three threshold) gains a step running this module's pytest.

## Out of scope

- Changing the cron schedule (`0 21 * * 0`) or the issue labels.
- Adding auto-remediation (the issue's `Remediation` section stays a human-actionable runbook link).
- Tightening the canonical projection (e.g. ignoring rule-list order). #30 / #116 considered this and intentionally rejected it; preserve behaviour.

## Verify

- `uv run --group dev pytest tests/test_ruleset_drift.py -v` passes locally.
- `gh workflow run ruleset-drift.yml --ref main` produces identical `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` shape to a pre-refactor run.
- Negative test: stage a one-field drift in `.github/rulesets/main.json` on a throwaway branch, force a dispatch -> exactly one SoT-drift issue filed, body matches snapshot.
- Negative test: stage an unknown live ruleset (via dispatch of `apply-rulesets.yml` with a name not in SoT — gate by environment first), confirm exactly one unknown-ruleset issue filed.

- Workflow origin: #30; delivered by #116.
- Sibling concern: #120 (PR-time `required_status_checks` sync — orthogonal axis).
- CLAUDE.md §3 — deterministic detector; §4 — abort loudly on ambiguous duplicates.

Sub-issue of #123 (priority 4 of 5 — first mutating workflow; gated by `environment: ruleset-apply`). Mirrors the pattern proved by #112 -> #122.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml` (originated by #18) carries ~170 lines of inline bash across `Plan and apply rulesets` + `Enable auto-delete head branches` + `Auto-delete (dry-run plan)` that:

1. Map the `ruleset` input choice (`all-branches`/`main`/`both`) to a list of SoT files.
2. Fetch live rulesets via `GET /repos/.../rulesets`; classify each SoT file as POST-new vs PUT-update vs ambiguous (multiple matches -> abort).
3. For PUT cases, fetch the existing live body and emit a `diff -u` block in the step summary.
4. Apply via POST or PUT with a hand-rolled 3-attempt retry loop (5xx + curl-level "000" only; 4xx breaks early).
5. Toggle `delete_branch_on_merge` repo setting via PATCH; emit before/after status.

This is the **first mutating** workflow in this refactor strategy. The retry logic and the POST/PUT decision are pure transformations of inputs; the diff rendering is `difflib.unified_diff`. Today none of it can be unit-tested.

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/rulesets_apply.py` (new)

Pure functions:
- `select_targets(choice: Literal["all-branches", "main", "both"]) -> list[str]` — returns the ordered list of SoT filenames.
- `decide_action(sot_name: str, live: list[dict]) -> dict` — returns `{"action": "POST"|"PUT"|"ambiguous", "live_id": int|None, "match_count": int}`.
- `canonical_projection(ruleset: dict) -> dict` — same as `ruleset_drift.py` (extract to a shared helper only after the third use site; #123 §"Risks" rule-of-three).
- `render_diff_section(name: str, live_id: int, live: dict, sot: dict) -> str` — Markdown `` block.
- `render_summary_row(file: str, name: str, matches: int, action: str, live_id: str | None, result: str) -> str`.

Side-effect wrappers (mockable):
- `fetch_live_rulesets(repo: str, token: str, *, opener=urllib.request.urlopen) -> list[dict]`.
- `fetch_live_ruleset(repo: str, ruleset_id: int, token: str, *, opener=...) -> dict`.
- `apply_call(*, method: str, url: str, payload_path: Path | None, token: str, opener=..., sleeper=time.sleep) -> tuple[int, str]` — 3-attempt retry with exponential backoff; returns `(http_code, response_body)`. Sleeper is overridable for tests (don't actually sleep in pytest).
- `get_repo_setting(repo: str, key: str, token: str, *, opener=...) -> Any` / `patch_repo_setting(repo: str, payload: dict, token: str, *, opener=...) -> None`.

CLI:
- `python3 scripts/rulesets_apply.py plan --repo OWNER/NAME --sot-dir .github/rulesets --choice CHOICE --summary-file PATH` — read + classify + render diff; **no live writes**.
- `python3 scripts/rulesets_apply.py apply --repo OWNER/NAME --sot-dir .github/rulesets --choice CHOICE --summary-file PATH` — plan + write; preserves exit-on-first-failure semantic.
- `python3 scripts/rulesets_apply.py auto-delete --repo OWNER/NAME --dry-run BOOL --summary-file PATH` — toggle `delete_branch_on_merge`.

### `tests/test_rulesets_apply.py` (new, target: ~45 cases)

- `TestSelectTargets` — each of `all-branches`/`main`/`both`; rejects unknown input with `ValueError`.
- `TestDecideAction` — POST when match_count=0; PUT when match_count=1; ambiguous when match_count>1 (and that's the failure path).
- `TestCanonicalProjection` — six fields preserved; ordering stable.
- `TestRenderDiffSection` — `` shape, diff block format, no diff -> empty diff body (but the section is still rendered for PUT cases — preserve current behaviour).
- `TestRenderSummaryRow` — empty `live_id` renders as `—`; HTTP code renders correctly.
- `TestApplyCall happy path` — single attempt 2xx returns immediately; sleeper not called.
- `TestApplyCall retry on 5xx` — 500 -> 500 -> 200 succeeds; sleeper called with `5, 10` (the existing backoff schedule from `ATTEMPT * 5`).
- `TestApplyCall break on 4xx` — 422 returns immediately, no retry, exit nonzero.
- `TestApplyCall curl-level failure ("000")` — retries up to 3 attempts.
- `TestApplyCall max attempts exhausted` — returns final code, caller exits.
- `TestFetchLiveRulesets` — auth header included; 401 raises.
- `TestCLI plan` — clean SoT all-new (3 POSTs planned); mixed POST+PUT; ambiguous live blocks the run.
- `TestCLI apply` — dry-run-equivalent via mocked `apply_call`; assert the right URL / method / payload-path per file.
- `TestCLI auto-delete` — dry-run prints current; live-apply emits before/after.

### `.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml`

All three mutating steps collapse to single Python invocations. `RULESETS_PAT`, `environment: ruleset-apply`, `Guard dispatch ref` step, and `Validate ruleset JSON syntax` step all unchanged (the last one can stay shell — `jq empty` is trivial and not in the refactor scope per #123's "minimum bash per workflow" target).

### `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`

The `lint-scripts` job (renamed from `lint-uv-pin` per #123's rule-of-three) gains this module's pytest.

## Out of scope

- Changing retry backoff (`5s, 10s` for attempts 2-3) or attempt count (3). Preserve behaviour.
- Replacing curl with PyGithub or `httpx`. Stays `urllib.request`.
- Centralising the retry helper. Defer until apply-labels (#5) lands and confirms three call sites.
- Adding new safety gates (e.g. requiring `dry_run=true` first). Operational concern, separate issue.

## Verify

- `uv run --group dev pytest tests/test_rulesets_apply.py -v` passes locally.
- Dispatch `apply-rulesets.yml` with `dry_run=true, ruleset=both` — `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` matches pre-refactor shape exactly (compare via run UI).
- Dispatch with `dry_run=false` against a no-op SoT change — applies succeed, summary correctly shows `PUT applied | HTTP 200`.
- Negative test: introduce a duplicate live ruleset name (one-shot via `gh api`), dispatch -> aborts with "Multiple existing rulesets named ''" before any write.

5. Toggle `delete_branch_on_merge` repo setting via PATCH; emit before/after status.

### `scripts/rulesets_apply.py` (new)

- `decide_action(sot_name: str, live: list[dict]) -> dict` -- returns `{"action": "POST"|"PUT"|"ambiguous", "live_id": int|None, "match_count": int}`.
- `canonical_projection(ruleset: dict) -> dict` -- same as `ruleset_drift.py` (extract to a shared helper only after the third use site; #123 S"Risks" rule-of-three).
- `render_diff_section(name: str, live_id: int, live: dict, sot: dict) -> str` -- Markdown `` block.
- `render_summary_row(file: str, name: str, matches: int, action: str, live_id: str | None, result: str) -> str`.

- `fetch_live_rulesets(repo: str, token: str, *, opener=urllib.request.urlopen) -> list[dict]`.
- `fetch_live_ruleset(repo: str, ruleset_id: int, token: str, *, opener=...) -> dict`.
- `apply_call(*, method: str, url: str, payload_path: Path | None, token: str, opener=..., sleeper=time.sleep) -> tuple[int, str]` -- 3-attempt retry with exponential backoff; returns `(http_code, response_body)`. Sleeper is overridable for tests (don't actually sleep in pytest).

- `TestDecideAction` -- POST when match_count=0; PUT when match_count=1; ambiguous when match_count>1 (and that's the failure path).
- `TestCanonicalProjection` -- six fields preserved; ordering stable.
- `TestRenderDiffSection` -- `` shape, diff block format, no diff -> empty diff body (but the section is still rendered for PUT cases -- preserve current behaviour).
- `TestRenderSummaryRow` -- empty `live_id` renders as `--`; HTTP code renders correctly.
- `TestApplyCall happy path` -- single attempt 2xx returns immediately; sleeper not called.
- `TestApplyCall retry on 5xx` -- 500 -> 500 -> 200 succeeds; sleeper called with `5, 10` (the existing backoff schedule from `ATTEMPT * 5`).
- `TestApplyCall break on 4xx` -- 422 returns immediately, no retry, exit nonzero.

## Symptom (fact)

`.github/workflows/apply-labels.yml` (originated by #34/#84) carries ~160 lines of inline bash in `Plan and apply labels` that:

1. Fetch live labels via `GET /repos/.../labels?per_page=100` (with a hard fail if `length >= 100` — pagination not implemented).
2. Pass 1 — for each SoT label, compare against live: POST if missing; PATCH if color or description differs; no-op if both match.
3. Pass 2 — for each live label not in SoT: report-only when `prune=false`; DELETE when `prune=true` (and `dry_run=false`).
4. All API calls go through an inlined `apply_call()` shell function with a 3-attempt retry, exponential backoff (`ATTEMPT * 5`), 4xx-breaks-early, 5xx-retries semantic — **a structural duplicate** of `apply-rulesets.yml`'s retry block.
5. Step-summary table generated row-by-row with per-row action + diff annotations + HTTP code or `dry-run` placeholder.

The reconciliation algebra (POST vs PATCH vs no-op vs DELETE-or-skip) is the most intricate of all five workflows — and the retry helper is the third call site (after `ruleset-drift` fetch + `rulesets-apply` apply), which crosses the **rule-of-three threshold** for extracting a shared `scripts/_github_api.py` helper (per #123's "Risks" section).

## Scope of fix

### `scripts/labels_apply.py` (new)

Pure functions:
- `validate_sot(sot: list[dict]) -> None` — asserts every entry has `name` (str, non-empty), `color` (hex), `description` (str, ≤100 chars); raises `ValueError` with the offending name on failure (mirrors the existing `description | length > 100` jq check).
- `decide_label_action(*, sot_entry: dict, live_entry: dict | None) -> dict` — returns `{"action": "POST"|"PATCH"|"NOOP", "method": str, "url_suffix": str, "payload": dict | None, "color_changed": bool, "desc_changed": bool}`.
- `decide_prune_action(*, live_name: str, in_sot: bool, prune: bool, dry_run: bool) -> Literal["skip", "report", "plan-delete", "delete"]`.
- `render_action_row(name: str, action: str, color_changed: str, desc_changed: str, result: str) -> str`.

Side-effect wrappers (mockable):
- `fetch_live_labels(repo: str, token: str, *, opener=urllib.request.urlopen) -> list[dict]` — includes the `length >= 100` guard with the documented error message.
- `apply_call(*, method: str, url: str, payload: dict | None, token: str, opener=..., sleeper=time.sleep) -> tuple[int, str]` — **moved into `scripts/_github_api.py` as a shared helper** (rule of three crossed; see #123 Risks); imported by `labels_apply.py` and `rulesets_apply.py`. Behaviour byte-identical to the bash version: 3 attempts, sleep `ATTEMPT * 5`, retry on 5xx/`000`, break on 4xx.

CLI:

- `python3 scripts/labels_apply.py apply --repo OWNER/NAME --sot .github/labels.json --prune BOOL --summary-file PATH` — plan + write; preserves exit-on-first-failure semantic.

### `scripts/_github_api.py` (new — extracted from this sub-issue, also imported by `rulesets_apply.py`)

Single function: `apply_call(...)` per the signature above. Tests live in `tests/test_github_api.py` (covers retry behaviour exhaustively so neither caller needs to repeat it). - `TestDecideLabelAction` — POST when live is None; PATCH when color differs; PATCH when description differs; PATCH when both differ; NOOP when both match; empty live description treated as `""` (matches current `// ""` fallback).
- `TestDecidePruneAction` — every cell of the `(in_sot, prune, dry_run)` truth table.
- `TestRenderActionRow` — pipe-escape in label names; HTTP code formatting; em-dash placeholders for irrelevant cells.
- `TestFetchLiveLabels` — happy path; `length >= 100` triggers documented error; auth header included.
- `TestCLI plan` — all-new SoT (3 POSTs planned); mixed POST/PATCH/NOOP; pruning planned when `prune=true`; pruning suppressed when `prune=false` (report-only row).

- `TestApplyCall happy 2xx` — single attempt; sleeper not called.
- `TestApplyCall retry 5xx -> 5xx -> 2xx` — sleeper called with `5, 10`.
- `TestApplyCall break on 4xx` — single attempt; returns the 422 immediately; no retry.
- `TestApplyCall curl-level "000"` — retries up to 3 attempts.
- `TestApplyCall all attempts fail` — returns the final code; caller responsible for exit.
- `TestApplyCall payload None vs dict` — both forms produce correct request body.

The 160-line `Plan and apply labels` step collapses to two Python invocations (plan + apply, or just `apply` which internally plans-then-writes). `Validate labels.json JSON syntax` and `Validate labels.json description length` shell steps fold into `labels_apply.py validate` (or stay as `jq` one-liners — operator choice).

### `.github/workflows/verify-agents.yml`

`lint-scripts` job (already renamed by sub-issue #3 or #4) gains both `tests/test_labels_apply.py` and `tests/test_github_api.py`.

## Out of scope

- Adding pagination to `fetch_live_labels` (the current `length >= 100` guard already surfaces the limit loudly per CLAUDE.md §4; pagination is a separate concern, file if/when the label count actually approaches 100).
- Changing retry backoff or attempt count.

Refs #123 (sub-issue 1 of 5).

## Context

`.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml` carries ~30 LOC of inline bash that strips HTML comments from a PR body, regex-extracts `Refs|Closes|Fixes|Resolves #N` references, and verifies each `#N` resolves via `gh api`. Per #123, inline YAML shell is untestable and violates CLAUDE.md section 3 (deterministic harness). #112 -> #122 established the precedent: pure logic moves to `scripts/*.py` with pytest coverage; the workflow shells out to the entry point.

This sub-issue is first in #123's priority order because it is the smallest (~30 LOC), read-only (no GitHub writes), and the side-effect surface is a single `gh api` GET — the lowest blast-radius candidate to iterate the testing pattern on.

## Scope of fix

Mirrors `scripts/uv_pin.py` + `tests/test_uv_pin.py` shape.

1. New `scripts/issue_link.py` with pure functions and an argparse CLI:
   - `strip_html_comments(body: str) -> str` -- Python equivalent of `perl -0777 -pe 's///gs'` using `re.sub` with DOTALL + non-greedy.
   - `extract_refs(body: str) -> list[int]` -- case-insensitive multiline match of `^\s*(Refs|Closes|Fixes|Resolves)\s+#(\d+)`, sorted-unique ints. Composes with `strip_html_comments` so HTML-commented refs are not picked up.
   - `issue_exists(repo: str, number: int) -> bool` -- thin `subprocess.run(["gh", "api", f"/repos/{repo}/issues/{number}", "--silent"])` wrapper; returns False on any subprocess failure (mirrors `uv_pin.fetch_latest_uv_release()` pattern).
   - CLI: `python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo "$REPO"` reads `PR_BODY` from env (matches the workflow's existing contract), prints `OK: #N resolves...` / `::error::Referenced #N does not exist...` / `::error::PR body has no issue reference...`, exits 0 or 1.

2. New `tests/test_issue_link.py` covering:
   - `strip_html_comments`: empty body, no comments, single-line comment, multi-line comment, multiple comments, comment containing the keyword (must not survive into `extract_refs`).
   - `extract_refs`: each keyword case-insensitively (`refs`, `REFS`, `Refs`, `Closes`, `Fixes`, `Resolves`), single ref, multiple refs (sorted-unique), leading whitespace allowed, mid-line `Refs #5` rejected (anchor `^`), `Reference #5` rejected (word boundary on keyword), HTML-commented ref skipped after composition, no refs found.
   - `issue_exists`: success (return True), `subprocess.CalledProcessError` non-zero (False), `FileNotFoundError` (False), `TimeoutExpired` (False) -- monkeypatched per `test_uv_pin.TestFetchLatestUvRelease`.
   - CLI: happy path with one resolvable ref, no refs (exit 1, `::error::` message), one resolvable + one missing (exit 1), missing `PR_BODY` env (exit 1 or treat as empty -- decide during impl).

3. `.github/workflows/verify-issue-link.yml` collapses to a single `python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo "$REPO"` step. Inline LOC drops from ~30 to under 10 (just the step shell-out + env marshalling).

4. `verify-agents.yml` already runs `python3 -m pytest -v`; `tests/test_issue_link.py` is auto-picked up via `testpaths = ["tests"]` in `pyproject.toml`. No new CI wiring needed (#112 already paved that path).

## Out of scope

- Behaviour change. Same exit codes, same `::error::` annotation strings, same stdout (modulo Python-vs-bash formatting if it matches the spec literally).
- Migrating to PyGithub / githubkit (#123: stdlib + subprocess preferred until a sub-issue's tests outgrow that).
- Shared HTTP retry helper. `issue_exists` does a single GET, so no retry logic exists to deduplicate yet -- rule of three (#123).
- The other 4 sub-issues of #123 (branch-cleanup, ruleset-drift, apply-rulesets, apply-labels).

## Verify

- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_issue_link.py -v` -- all cases green.
- Manually exercise the CLI against the live repo with a PR body that references a known issue:
  - `PR_BODY="Refs #123" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 0 and prints `OK: #123 resolves in tvna/claude-md.`
  - `PR_BODY="" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 1 with the no-ref error.
  - `PR_BODY="Refs #999999" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 1 with the missing-ref error.
- Confirm the existing `Verify issue link` workflow runs green on the PR that lands this refactor (self-verification).

## References

- Parent: #123.
- Precedent: #112 -> #118 + #122 (`scripts/uv_pin.py`, `tests/test_uv_pin.py`).
- Origin issue for the workflow: #110.
- CLAUDE.md section 3 (deterministic harness) and section 4 (fail loudly, no silent defaults).

   - `issue_exists(repo: str, number: int) -> bool` -- thin `subprocess.run(["gh", "api", f"/repos/{repo}/issues/{number}", "--silent"])` wrapper; returns False on any subprocess failure (mirrors `uv_pin.fetch_latest_uv_release()` pattern).
   - CLI: `python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo "$REPO"` reads `PR_BODY` from env (matches the workflow's existing contract), prints `OK: #N resolves...` / `::error::Referenced #N does not exist...` / `::error::PR body has no issue reference...`, exits 0 or 1.

2. New `tests/test_issue_link.py` covering:
   - `strip_html_comments`: empty body, no comments, single-line comment, multi-line comment, multiple comments, comment containing the keyword (must not survive into `extract_refs`).
   - `extract_refs`: each keyword case-insensitively (`refs`, `REFS`, `Refs`, `Closes`, `Fixes`, `Resolves`), single ref, multiple refs (sorted-unique), leading whitespace allowed, mid-line `Refs #5` rejected (anchor `^`), `Reference #5` rejected (word boundary on keyword), HTML-commented ref skipped after composition, no refs found.
   - `issue_exists`: success (return True), `subprocess.CalledProcessError` non-zero (False), `FileNotFoundError` (False), `TimeoutExpired` (False) -- monkeypatched per `test_uv_pin.TestFetchLatestUvRelease`.
   - CLI: happy path with one resolvable ref, no refs (exit 1, `::error::` message), one resolvable + one missing (exit 1), missing `PR_BODY` env (exit 1 or treat as empty -- decide during impl).

## Out of scope

- Behaviour change. Same exit codes, same `::error::` annotation strings, same stdout (modulo Python-vs-bash formatting if it matches the spec literally).
- Migrating to PyGithub / githubkit (#123: stdlib + subprocess preferred until a sub-issue's tests outgrow that).
- Shared HTTP retry helper. `issue_exists` does a single GET, so no retry logic exists to deduplicate yet -- rule of three (#123).
- The other 4 sub-issues of #123 (branch-cleanup, ruleset-drift, apply-rulesets, apply-labels).

## Verify

- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_issue_link.py -v` -- all cases green.
- Manually exercise the CLI against the live repo with a PR body that references a known issue:
  - `PR_BODY="Refs #123" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 0 and prints `OK: #123 resolves in tvna/claude-md.`
  - `PR_BODY="" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 1 with the no-ref error.
  - `PR_BODY="Refs #999999" python3 scripts/issue_link.py verify --repo tvna/claude-md` exits 1 with the missing-ref error.
- Confirm the existing `Verify issue link` workflow runs green on the PR that lands this refactor (self-verification).

## References

- Parent: #123.
- Precedent: #112 -> #118 + #122 (`scripts/uv_pin.py`, `tests/test_uv_pin.py`).
- Origin issue for the workflow: #110.
- CLAUDE.md section 3 (deterministic harness) and section 4 (fail loudly, no silent defaults).
